chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from 'Abd Allah, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, Zurarah ibn A'yan, Bukayr ibn A'yan, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah al-'Ijli, who said: He said:

Abu Ja'far عليه السلام and Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: The time of Zuhr after zawal is two feet, and the time of 'Asr after that is two feet. And this is the beginning of the time, until four feet pass for 'Asr.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The way to reconcile these reports and the earlier reports is that what they contain of the wording of the foot, the cubit, and the stature was only mentioned with respect to the نافلة, because when the sun declines, the time of the salat has entered. However, it is recommended that one begin first with the supererogatory prayer until the shadow becomes two feet. When it becomes so, then the time of the نافلة has passed and the time of the obligatory prayer has become constrained. So these measures—namely the cubit, the stature, and the two statures—were set with respect to the نافلة, not that they are not a time for the obligatory prayer. And that which indicates this detail is...

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: the sun’s decline from the meridian, marking entry of prayer time
key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: the supererogatory prayer performed in addition to the obligatory prayer
key_terms.الْفَيْءِ: the returning shadow used as a timing indicator
key_terms.الْقَدَمِ: a measured unit used here for determining preferred timing
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the appointed time of an act of worship

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith explain the beginning time of Zuhr and 'Asr prayer after zawal?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the beginning times of Zuhr and 'Asr and explains reports that mention measurements such as a foot, cubit, and stature. The compiler clarifies that these measures relate to the preferred time for the supererogatory prayer before the obligatory salat, while the obligatory prayer time itself begins at zawal.
